input.summary:
Guest bath designed and written in parts/room-7.mjs: a three-cell water tub on the south wall (focal, in view from the door), a planks vanity with basin cauldron and flower pot on the east wall, a linen barrel with a standing lantern by the door, and a hanging lantern over the tub.
On a bare test grid the light is 8 to 15 with no dark or dim cells, and the lane x36 z54..59 is clear; the walk check can't pass there because no corridor is built in that test.
NOT in build.nbt: every write is refused by runParts because shell.mjs:27 fills the whole interior with air and runParts locks air too, so no room part can place anything yet.
left: Blocked by the shell's air lock: shell.mjs:27 (`box()` fills the interior with "air") makes runParts refuse all room writes, including mine (10 refused on make.sh). Fix belongs to the shell or to runParts (lock only non-air placements); I did not bypass it.

Walk verdict unverified in the real build: the test grid had no corridor or doorway floor, so 'no way in' is expected there; re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "guest bath"` once the lock is fixed and the corridor is built.
Light and layout were checked only on the bare test grid (/tmp/part14-test/bare.nbt), not in build.nbt.
The guest bath item in elements.md (Bathrooms x5) and plan.md's checklist are not ticked: the bath is designed but not in the saved build, and the bathrooms item covers five rooms.

waste.what: Diagnosing why every write was refused: I read runParts and shell.mjs by hand and wrote a peek script to see which earlier part owned the bath cells.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and 3 minutes of reading
waste.tool: make.sh should print the earlier part's name next to each REFUSED cell (e.g. 'shell:box fill'), or `mcd check` should flag an air fill that locks the interior.

waste.what: Hand-indexing rows of a 3-wide layers() draft: I put a barrel in the lane (x36) and a cauldron on the wrong z row, and had to fix both by hand.
waste.cost: 2 retries of the draft, about 6 cell rows counted by eye
waste.tool: a `mcd plan` variant that prints the layers() draft back as a 3D ASCII view of the room, so rows and layers can be checked against the room box before writing.

waste.what: Light and walk checks needed a bare test grid of my own (walls, floors, doorway built by hand), because the real grid's rooms were locked.
waste.tool: `mcd room --bare` or a scratch-grid option that runs one room's build on empty walls so the room check works before the shell is finished.

companions.task: Run the water supply to the tub and the basin cauldron and check the drain side of the vanity; I used water_cauldron for the tub and an empty cauldron for the basin, and a plumber would confirm which is right for the fit-out.
